name: Skyviewer Explorer (Rubin Observatory)
oneLine: Rubin Observatory's deep-zoom sky explorer: one full-bleed survey image, a few floating circular controls, zero chrome.

palette.note: 48px top bar (hamburger left, close X right) and the deep-space backdrop of the survey image
Body background, near-black with a hint of green, shown while the canvas loads (fills the whole mobile capture)
Translucent charcoal 48px circular buttons: compass/globe, markers, grid, zoom +/-, fullscreen, share
Light-grey circular search button, top left; the one inverted control so search stands out
Icon strokes and body text color
Electric cyan pill banner at bottom center ('You are looking at ~1/10 of Rubin's field of view') with dark #1F2121 text

type.note: 17.5px regular with 700 bold for key figures ('~1/10'), sentence case; the only text on screen is the banner
Loaded as a fallback in the font stack for localized UI; not visible in the captures

layout: The layout is 100% image with no scrolling. The two scroll captures are identical to the hero, confirming a single fixed viewport where the data is the whole interface.

Controls are 48px circles floating over the image, grouped by job: search alone top left, navigation tools (compass, markers, grid) in a column top right, zoom +/- at mid right, fullscreen and share bottom left.
One cyan pill banner at bottom center gives scale context, and a small 'Aladin' credit sits bottom right. Every other pixel is the dataset.
motion: (inferred) Deep-zoom pan and pinch through a HiPS tile pyramid rendered with WebGL by Aladin Lite (2 canvases detected). Tiles sharpen progressively as you zoom, so the motion comes from direct manipulation.
(inferred) Search 'flies' the view to a named object with an eased pan-and-zoom, the signature motion of sky viewers.
The mobile capture shows only the flat #1F2121 loading surface under the black bar. The heavy canvas had not painted yet, a sign the first frame costs a lot.
interactions: Drag to pan and scroll or pinch to zoom across a gigapixel survey image, with circular zoom buttons as a fallback.
Search an object or coordinates, then toggle overlays (markers, coordinate grid) from the right-hand tool column.
A dismissible context banner gives a sense of scale; share and fullscreen sit bottom left.
steal: Telemetry explorer page: a full-bleed, chrome-free pan/zoom view of a multi-channel time series, with controls as 48px translucent floating circles grouped by job.
Explorer footer: a single cyan context pill ('You are viewing 3 of 76 channels, Mission 1, 2004–2006') that anchors scale without adding a panel.
Site-wide color rule: near-black #1F2121-style ground with one electric cyan accent, saved for the 'show anomaly' primary action (matching our accent-only-for-primary rule).
leave: The blank mobile first paint: shipping a heavy WebGL canvas with no poster or skeleton leaves phones on an empty grey screen. We need a static preview frame first.
Unlabeled icon-only controls (globe, diamond grid) are fine for astronomers but opaque to recruiters. Add tooltips or short labels.
